Source: IBGE PIB dos Municípios, SIDRA Tabela 5938, variable 37 (PIB a
preços correntes, mil reais), SIDRA agregados API v3, queried 2026-10-09
(`_data/raw/ibge/sidra/sidra_5938_pib_*.json`); IBGE censuses 1970-2010
and 2022, resident population (`_data/raw/ibge/Ibge_pop_1970-80-91-00-10.xlsx`,
`Ibge_pop_2022 (Censo - Sidra).xlsx`); IBGE annual population estimates,
SIDRA Tabela 6579 (`sidra_6579_pop_estimate_*.json`, read by the pipeline
since phase 2, step 2.5); the post-2000 municipality lookup
(`_data/aux/munic_post2000.csv`); IPCA deflator
(`_data/aux/deflator_ipca_2024.csv`).
Pipeline script: `_scripts/03-controls-gdp.R`.
Interim outputs: `_data/interim/ibge_pop_2000_2022.rds`,
`_data/interim/ibge_pib_gdp_2002_2022.rds`.
Equivalence with the recovered panel is not checked here (the notebook never
reads `_data/reference/`); the `compare_outputs` report lives in the phase 1
script 03 commit message and in the decision entries it cites.

```{r setup}
#| include: false
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = normalizePath(".."))
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(tidyverse)
  library(readxl)
})
options(width = 110)
```

```{r read}
source("_scripts/utils/read_sidra.R")
source("_scripts/utils/interpolate_census.R")
sidra_dir <- "_data/raw/ibge/sidra"
sidra <- function(pattern) {
  map_dfr(list.files(sidra_dir, pattern = pattern, full.names = TRUE), read_sidra_json)
}
pib_raw <- sidra("^sidra_5938_pib_")
est_raw <- sidra("^sidra_6579_pop_estimate_")
pop_0010_raw <- read_excel("_data/raw/ibge/Ibge_pop_1970-80-91-00-10.xlsx", sheet = "Tabela",
                           col_types = "text")
pop_2022_raw <- read_excel("_data/raw/ibge/Ibge_pop_2022 (Censo - Sidra).xlsx", sheet = "Tabela",
                           col_types = "text", col_names = FALSE, .name_repair = "minimal")
pop <- read_rds("_data/interim/ibge_pop_2000_2022.rds")
post2000 <- read_csv("_data/aux/munic_post2000.csv",
                     col_types = cols(.default = col_character(), install_year = col_integer()))
# Since step 2.5 the GDP file carries no population; it is joined here from
# its own file so the questions below read as before.
gdp <- read_rds("_data/interim/ibge_pib_gdp_2002_2022.rds") %>%
  left_join(pop %>% select(geocode, year, population, pop_source), by = c("geocode", "year"))
sample_geo <- read_rds("_data/interim/mapbiomas_deforestation_amz_1987_2023.rds") %>%
  distinct(geocode, municipality, state_abbreviation)
is_geocode <- function(x) !is.na(x) & str_detect(x, "^[0-9]{7}$")
```

## Q1. What do the GDP extracts contain?

What is checked: files, series count, year span, unit, symbols, and the
sample cells without a value.

```{r q1-shape}
list.files(sidra_dir, pattern = "^sidra_5938_pib_")
pib_raw %>%
  summarise(series = n_distinct(geocode), years = paste(range(year), collapse = "-"),
            cells = n(), dots = sum(value == "..."), negative = sum(str_detect(value, "^-")),
            other = sum(!str_detect(value, "^-?[0-9]+$") & value != "..."))
pib_raw %>% filter(str_detect(value, "^-"))
pib_raw %>%
  filter(geocode %in% sample_geo$geocode, value == "...") %>%
  left_join(sample_geo, by = "geocode") %>%
  group_by(geocode, municipality.y, state_abbreviation) %>%
  summarise(years = paste(range(year), collapse = "-"), n = n(), .groups = "drop")
```

**Finding.** Eight files cover 2002-2023 for the 5,570 municipalities, in
integer thousands of reais (the lost CSV export carried decimals,
D-2026-10-10-b). The only symbol is "..."; one cell is negative (Guamaré,
RN, 2012, as published by IBGE, outside the sample). In the sample the
missing cells are Ipiranga do Norte and Itanhangá (MT) for 2002-2004, the
years before their installation, and Mojuí dos Campos (PA) for 2002-2012,
which the pipeline fills by the Santarém split (Q3).
**Decision.** D-2026-10-10-b; D-2026-10-10-g.
**Assertion.** `03-controls-gdp.R`, raw-state block (no classification,
5,570 series, symbols, one negative value).

## Q2. What do the population workbooks contain?

```{r q2-layout}
names(pop_0010_raw)
nrow(pop_0010_raw)
pop_0010_raw %>% summarise(across(c(`2000`, `2010`), ~ sum(.x == "...")))
pop_0010_raw %>% filter(`2010` == "...")
as.data.frame(pop_2022_raw[1:6, ])
geo_2022 <- pop_2022_raw[[2]][is_geocode(pop_2022_raw[[2]])]
length(geo_2022)
setdiff(geo_2022, pop_0010_raw$munic_id)
```

```{r q2-sample-2000}
pop_0010_raw %>%
  filter(munic_id %in% sample_geo$geocode, `2000` == "...") %>%
  select(munic_id, munic, `2000`, `2010`)
```

**Finding.** The 1970-2010 workbook has one row per municipality of the
2010 grid plus Cococi (CE), an extinct municipality with no value; "..."
marks the censuses before a municipality existed, 59 cells in 2000. The
2022 workbook (Tabela 4709) has four header rows, a Brasil row, 5,570
municipal rows and a source footer; five municipalities installed in 2013
appear only there, Mojuí dos Campos among them. In the sample the nine
Mato Grosso municipalities of task 1.6 have no 2000 value.
**Decision.** D-2026-10-05-f (interpolation between the anchors);
D-2026-10-05-k (consequence for the nine); D-2026-10-10-g.
**Assertion.** `03-controls-gdp.R`, raw-state block (column names, 5,566
rows, 2022 header cells, 5,570 municipalities in 2022, anchors positive).

## Q3. What do Santarém and Mojuí dos Campos carry before 2013?

What is checked: the pair's stored GDP and population around 2013, and
Santarém's stored GDP against the served value. Until phase 2, step 2.5
(2026-10-23) the pipeline split Santarém's pre-2013 GDP and population
with Mojuí by the pair's 2022 shares (D-2026-10-10-e); since the step the
parent rule of task 1.6 applies (D-2026-10-23-f).

```{r q3-pair}
pair <- gdp %>%
  filter(geocode %in% c("1506807", "1504752"), year %in% c(2002, 2010:2014, 2022)) %>%
  select(geocode, year, population, pop_source, gdp_brl)
pair %>% pivot_wider(names_from = geocode, values_from = c(population, pop_source, gdp_brl))
santarem_raw <- pib_raw %>%
  filter(geocode == "1506807", year %in% c(2002, 2010:2014, 2022)) %>%
  transmute(year, santarem_served = as.numeric(value) * 1000)
pair %>%
  filter(geocode == "1506807") %>%
  inner_join(santarem_raw, by = "year") %>%
  mutate(diff = gdp_brl - santarem_served) %>%
  select(year, gdp_brl, santarem_served, diff)
```

**Finding.** Santarém's stored GDP equals the served value in every
year, and its population is the published anchors interpolated: the 2000
and 2010 values include the territory that became Mojuí and the 2022
value does not, so the 2010-2022 segment slopes toward a smaller
territory (the parent-rule bias task 1.6 names; flagged in script 04,
not corrected). Mojuí is NA before 2013 in GDP (served as "...") and in
population (not installed), carries the official estimates for 2013-2021
and its 2022 census count.
**Decision.** D-2026-10-23-f (supersedes D-2026-10-10-e).
**Assertion.** `03-controls-gdp.R`, output block (a lookup municipality
is NA before its installation year and complete from it, in population
and in GDP).

## Q4. Which municipalities lack GDP per capita before 2010, and what do the official estimates say?

What is checked: the sample municipalities with NA population in the GDP
years, and the Tabela 6579 estimates for the same municipality-years.

```{r q4-missing}
gdp %>%
  filter(geocode %in% sample_geo$geocode, is.na(population)) %>%
  left_join(sample_geo, by = "geocode") %>%
  group_by(geocode, municipality, state_abbreviation) %>%
  summarise(years = paste(range(year), collapse = "-"), n = n(),
            gdp_present = sum(!is.na(gdp_brl)), .groups = "drop")
```

```{r q4-estimates}
list.files(sidra_dir, pattern = "^sidra_6579_")
est <- est_raw %>% transmute(geocode, year, estimate = sidra_value(value, character(0)))
gdp %>%
  filter(geocode == "5103254", year <= 2012) %>%
  select(year, population, gdp_brl) %>%
  left_join(est %>% filter(geocode == "5103254") %>% select(year, estimate), by = "year")
```

**Finding.** The nine Mato Grosso municipalities installed after 2000 have
GDP from 2002 (seven of them) or 2005 (Ipiranga do Norte, Itanhangá) but,
until phase 2, step 2.5 (2026-10-23), no population before 2010, so their
GDP per capita was NA for 2002-2009 and Colniza dropped from every
covariate-adjusted specification (D-2026-10-05-k). Tabela 6579 carries
official estimates for 2001-2006, 2008-2009, 2011-2021 and 2024 onward
(2007 was a population count, 2010 and 2022 censuses, 2023 is not
served) for every one of them from their installation; since the step
they are spliced in (Q7) and the first table above is empty.
**Decision.** D-2026-10-05-k (closed at step 2.5 by D-2026-10-23-e).
**Assertion.** `03-controls-gdp.R`, output block (population NA only
before the first census that counts the municipality, or before the
installation year for a lookup municipality).

## Q5. How far is the interpolated population from the official estimates?

```{r q5-deviation}
gdp %>%
  filter(geocode %in% sample_geo$geocode, !is.na(population)) %>%
  inner_join(est, by = c("geocode", "year")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(estimate)) %>%
  mutate(rel = population / estimate - 1) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), median_rel = median(rel), p10 = quantile(rel, 0.10),
            p90 = quantile(rel, 0.90), .groups = "drop")
```

**Finding.** Through 2009 the median deviation stays within one percent,
with the 10-90 range widening to about -17/+26 percent in the middle of
the decade, where a straight line between censuses departs most from the
estimated path. From 2011 the median drifts to -6.7 percent by 2021: the
line toward the 2022 census, which came in below the projected estimates,
runs under them, and the range reaches -26/+11 percent. The deviation is
the cost of D-2026-10-05-f, kept at step 2.5: the estimates enter only
where a municipality has no 2000 anchor (D-2026-10-23-e); the anchors
are stored at task 1.7.
**Decision.** D-2026-10-05-f (interpolation kept); D-2026-10-23-e.

## Q6. For which years is population stored?

```{r q6-years}
pop %>%
  filter(geocode %in% sample_geo$geocode) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), population_na = sum(is.na(population)),
            census = sum(pop_source == "census", na.rm = TRUE),
            census_interp = sum(pop_source == "census_interp", na.rm = TRUE),
            ibge_estimate = sum(pop_source == "ibge_estimate", na.rm = TRUE),
            estimate_interp = sum(pop_source == "estimate_interp", na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(year <= 2010 | year >= 2020)
gdp %>%
  filter(geocode %in% sample_geo$geocode) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), gdp_na = sum(is.na(gdp_brl)), per_capita_na = sum(is.na(gdp_per_capita)),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(year <= 2004 | year >= 2020)
```

**Finding.** Since phase 2, step 2.5 (2026-10-23) population is its own
series, 2000-2022 for every municipality, with the source of each cell;
until then it rode on the GDP rows and the panel had no population in
2000-2001 (D-2026-10-10-k). In the biome sample the only NA cells are the
post-2000 municipalities before installation (ten in 2000, three in 2001,
two through 2004: Mojuí dos Campos through 2012); GDP per capita is NA
only where GDP is. The 2023 GDP release is read and dropped by the year
cap; 2023-2024 population belongs to the anchor work of task 1.7.
**Decision.** D-2026-10-23-e (closes D-2026-10-10-k for 2000-2022).
**Assertion.** `03-controls-gdp.R`, output block (5,570 x 23 rows, source
NA exactly where population is, per-capita NA pattern).

## Q7. How are the official estimates spliced in for the municipalities installed after 2000?

What is checked: the stored population and its source for the nine sample
municipalities 2000-2012, the estimate path against the 2010 census, and
the pre-installation estimates Tabela 6579 serves.

```{r q7-splice}
est <- est_raw %>% transmute(geocode, year, estimate = sidra_value(value, character(0)))
pop %>%
  filter(geocode %in% post2000$geocode, year <= 2012) %>%
  left_join(post2000 %>% select(geocode, municipality, install_year), by = "geocode") %>%
  select(municipality, install_year, year, population, pop_source) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = c(population, pop_source), names_vary = "slowest") %>%
  select(municipality, install_year, starts_with("population_"))
pop %>%
  filter(geocode %in% post2000$geocode, year %in% c(2006, 2007, 2008, 2009, 2010)) %>%
  left_join(est, by = c("geocode", "year")) %>%
  left_join(post2000 %>% select(geocode, municipality), by = "geocode") %>%
  select(municipality, year, population, pop_source, estimate) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = c(population, estimate), names_vary = "slowest")
est %>%
  filter(geocode %in% post2000$geocode) %>%
  left_join(post2000 %>% select(geocode, municipality, install_year), by = "geocode") %>%
  filter(!is.na(estimate), year < install_year) %>%
  select(municipality, install_year, year, estimate)
```

**Finding.** Each lookup municipality is NA before its installation year,
carries the official estimate from that year to 2009 (2013-2021 for
Mojuí), and the interpolated census path from 2010. The 2007 count year,
not served, is interpolated between the 2006 and 2008 estimates. The
estimates of the 2001 cohort before the 2007 count are projections from a
base that did not enumerate the municipality: Colniza reads 14,149 in
2006 and 29,636 in 2008, and the other eight move by a few percent at the
same point in either direction; the 2009 estimates sit close to the 2010
census. Tabela 6579 also serves a 2004 estimate for Ipiranga do Norte and
Itanhangá, published before their installation in 2005 (the FPM quota of
the first year), which the rule does not use. A 2007 count (SIDRA Tabela
793) could replace the nine interpolated cells as a value-level change.
**Decision.** D-2026-10-23-e.
**Assertion.** `03-controls-gdp.R`, output block (NA before installation,
complete from it; nine `estimate_interp` cells, all 2007; census years
read `census`).
